title: Scientific verification: tiny-batch overfit protocol — scale-relative criteria, class-spanning batches, discriminating power, gradient-health semantics

problem.description: EXP-000008 (latest version v3, content of the v2 technical revision) claims: (1) the single-batch overfit test is a discriminator between mechanical bugs and convergence limits, not an absolute proof; (2) pass criteria must be scale-relative (100% batch accuracy; loss vs the ln(K) baseline and the memorization floor), never a fixed constant like loss<1e-2; (3) the tiny batch must span the classes — a single-class batch voids the test because a constant predictor wins it; (4) gradient checks verify FLOW not correctness, individual zero grads are normal (dead ReLUs, frozen params) and an all-nonzero-grad assertion is a false-positive generator; (5) the loss-dtype/logits expectations (e.g. CrossEntropyLoss) are doc-verifiable per framework version. This run executes the record's own embedded verification plan C1-C4, with C4 adapted to a pure-python MLP because no DL framework is installed on the workspace machine, plus a C4c capacity-boundary case added from design-iteration findings.
problem.symptoms: networks that never learn; hours of hyperparameter tuning against broken pipelines; false-positive gradient assertions; fixed loss thresholds misjudging good fits at large target scales
problem.expectedBehavior: C1: chance-level CE equals ln(K) exactly (K=2: 0.693147, K=10: 2.302585); near-one-hot correct-prediction CE approaches 0. C2: a constant predictor scores 100% on a single-class batch but exactly 1/K on a class-spanning batch. C4a: a finite-difference-verified healthy pure-python MLP (dh=4) reaches 100% batch accuracy with loss < 0.1*ln(4) within 400 steps at lr 0.5. C4b: the same architecture on independently shuffled labels fails the protocol even after 4x steps at raised LR (accuracy below 100%, loss above 0.1*ln4). C4c: at excess capacity (dh=16) the same budget fully memorizes the misaligned labels — documenting that the protocol's inference requires task-matched capacity (the record's own limitation note). C5: a fixed loss<1e-2 threshold false-fails a fully-fitted MSE problem at target scale 1000 (MSE~100 with R2>0.999) while passing the identical problem at scale 1 (MSE~1e-4). C6: a healthy memorizing pipeline with dead ReLU units carries exactly-zero grads on a large fraction of weights; the naive all-nonzero assertion fails (false positive) while the correct assertion (no NaN/Inf + every trainable layer has a nonzero grad) passes. C3: the official PyTorch documentation (version resolved live) states the CE loss expects unnormalized logits and long-dtype class-index targets.
problem.actualBehavior: to be measured by real execution on the user's machine through the bridge
problem.facts: -log(1/K) = ln(K); the CE floor of a fully memorizing classifier is ~0; MSE noise floors scale with the square of the target scale; ReLU units with negative pre-activations contribute exactly-zero gradients; excess-capacity networks can memorize random labels (Zhang et al. 2017), so the protocol's discriminating power depends on task-matched capacity — which the record's limitations section already mandates.
problem.assumptions: python3 3.14.4 on the user's machine; fixed seeds (random.Random) make every result deterministic and reproducible; a pure-python MLP substitutes the DL-framework variant of C4 (no framework installed); outbound HTTPS is available for the documentation check; identical results are expected from the VM dry-run environment (Python 3.12.16) and the target machine modulo floating-point formatting.
problem.environment: user's machine via the bridge extension: Linux, Python 3.14.4, numpy 2.3.5 present (unused — stdlib only), torch absent, git 2.53.0, sqlite3 3.46.1; VM dry-runs on Python 3.12.16
problem.constraints: stdlib-only experiments (math/random — no framework dependency); every case is non-destructive (no workspace files written; the doc check writes only to mktemp); outputs kept below the 20KB attempt truncation limit; the documentation case fetches only the official pytorch.org docs and is flagged requiresNetwork so it cannot run without explicit confirmation.

hypothesis.text: All eight cases pass their declared criteria on real execution: the analytic baselines are exact; the class-spanning requirement holds; a gradient-verified healthy pipeline passes the protocol while a label-misaligned copy fails it at task-matched capacity; excess capacity memorizes misaligned labels (boundary documented, not hidden); a fixed 1e-2 loss threshold is scale-dependent and false-fails a fully-fitted large-scale MSE problem; dead ReLU units produce zero grads in a healthy pipeline, making the naive all-nonzero-grad assertion a false-positive generator; and the live-fetched PyTorch documentation confirms the logits/dtype expectations quoted in the record.
hypothesis.expectedObservation: each case prints its declared marker and exits 0: C1-BASELINES-VERIFIED, C2-CLASS-SPANNING-REQUIRED, C4a-HEALTHY-PIPELINE-VERIFIED, C4b-MECHANICAL-BUG-CORRECTLY-FLAGGED, C4c-CAPACITY-BOUNDARY-DOCUMENTED, C5-SCALE-RELATIVE-CRITERIA-REQUIRED, C6-ZERO-GRADS-NORMAL-CONFIRMED, C3-DOC-VERIFIED
hypothesis.supportingEvidence: VM-local dry-runs (Python 3.12.16) reproduce every marker; the FD gradient check max relative error 2.187e-09 certifies the pure-python implementation used as the known-healthy pipeline; design-iteration failures (capacity sensitivity, noise-vs-signal scaling bug in an early C5 draft) were caught locally and are reported in the analysis rather than hidden.
hypothesis.contradictingEvidence: none observed in dry-runs; the capacity sensitivity discovered during design iteration is converted into boundary case C4c instead of being suppressed.

strategy: Execute the record's own embedded verification plan: C1/C2 analytic baselines (exact math, deterministic), C4a/C4b protocol discriminating power on a finite-difference-certified pure-python MLP at task-matched capacity (dh=4), C4c the capacity boundary at dh=16, C5 fixed-threshold scale dependence via exact least squares at two target scales, C6 gradient-health semantics with dead ReLU units, C3 live documentation inspection (official PyTorch docs fetched from the user's machine). One case per claim class; all cases critical; the doc case is flagged requiresNetwork and executes only with explicit confirmation.
